column3: How can the principle on which this case is decided inform the remedy in Keron v Cashman? How wold you articulate this principle?

How does Locke's view on possession as the basis of property get applied (or not) in Pierson v Post? In what ways do the facts here complicate Locke's story about the connection between labour and property?
How does Armorie v Delamire further complicate Locke's story?
The relative nature of possession expressed in this case with respect to chattels (i.e. personal property like a jewel) also applies to land.
The decision in this case is related to common law principle mentioned in Pierson v Post, which establishes the suprior right of a landowner to property in wild animals capture on the owner's land.

If we believe Hale about the state's role in coersive enforcement as the basis of property, how should we interpret what was happening (or intended to happen) in the British Crown's grant of Rupter's Land to the Hudson Bay Company in 1670?

Against the background of cases like Pierson v Post, we might read Nova Scotia's Wildlife Act as a contemporary expression of Hale's perspective. What work is the the Wildlife Act doing with respect to the facts in our problem?

The two Peace and Friendship Treaties (1725 and 1752) we look at in this unit  should be read as part of a chain of international agreements during this period. In what ways are these treaties expressions of Hederson's perspective on the international dimensions of property and the relationship between plural legal orders?
